leads.summary: Endpoint-lightness Oklab/OkLCh entries render pink or dark red rather than white or black
leads.consequence: A copied valid `oklch(100% 0.2 0)` is shown with a pink [255,192,250] swatch rather than white, and `oklch(0% 0.2 0)` displays [7,0,0] instead of black. The same happens for `oklab(1 0.2 0)`. CSS Color 4 specifies endpoint lightness displays white/black due to gamut mapping; channel-wise RGB clipping after matrix conversion cannot do that. This can mislead when selecting a copied color; preserve endpoint behavior or implement CSS gamut mapping before Qt.rgba.

leads.summary: Negative OkLCh chroma produces a colored swatch instead of being clamped to zero
leads.consequence: CSS Color 4 allows a negative chroma and clamps it to 0 at parsed-value time; this code uses C unmodified in the polar-to-Cartesian conversion. Copying `oklch(0.6 -0.15 0)` gives a [0,156,132] teal swatch instead of the same neutral [128,128,128] swatch as `oklch(0.6 0 0)`. Clamp C before multiplying cos/sin, and add a negative-C fixture.

leads.summary: The shared argument splitter accepts non-CSS syntax and positive test fixtures enshrine one invalid form
leads.consequence: The splitter discards the distinction between CSS legacy comma and modern space/slash syntax. `rgb(100%, 0, 0)` mixes channel units in legacy form, `rgb(1 2 3 0.5)` omits the modern alpha slash, `hsla(0.5turn 50% 50%, 0.8)` mixes both separators, and `oklch(0.6, 0.15, 50)` adds forbidden commas; all receive swatches despite being invalid CSS colors. The test explicitly expects the invalid hsla form to pass. Validate per-function separator and alpha grammar, then replace the positive hsla fixture with a valid form and add negative cases.

leads.summary: Open PR #9892 also creates clipboard swatches and conflicts in the same QML delegate
leads.consequence: A true-common-base merge-file of the pinned heads has two conflicts at the delegate swatch property and text width. #9892 adds a model `required property string swatchColor`, `hasSwatch`, and a separate swatch Rectangle; #11667 adds a readonly property of the same name and another rectangle. Mechanically keeping both would duplicate the property and swatch, while choosing either width binding without reconsidering its logic can mis-size text. The other PR also intentionally changes the detail preview (not a fault in this PR). Coordinate feature ownership and choose one source of truth before both merge. GitHub reports #9892 individually MERGEABLE, which does not resolve this pair's conflict.

leads.summary: Open PR #9662's favorite star and the swatch both claim row width
leads.consequence: A merge-file at the pinned heads has two conflicting delegate hunks. #9662 reserves `row.starWidth` and places a star button at the right edge; #11667 reserves the color swatch width. Keeping only either width expression when resolving loses the other deduction, so a colored favorite row's text can run beneath the star or row contents can extend past their available width. Preserve both declarations and subtract both widths in the combined binding; QML fixtures have not been run on that manual resolution. GitHub reports #9662 individually MERGEABLE; the heads are diverged, not stacked.

leads.summary: Open PR #7452 requires manual conflict resolution at the history limit and empty-state text
leads.consequence: The pinned-head three-way merge has two conflict hunks. #7452 makes historyLimit configurable with a different default and changes the empty-state label for images-only mode; the older lines in #11667's head conflict with these. Do not overwrite #7452's two behaviors when reconciling the swatch feature. GitHub currently reports #7452 itself CONFLICTING, independent of this pair; this is a lower-priority coordination issue, not a claim that #11667 breaks its intended swatch behavior.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** One low-impact false positive: bare 8-digit strings such as dates, numbers and short hashes get a swatch, and dates come out almost fully transparent.

### Bare 8-digit strings are read as RRGGBBAA

`parseHex` accepts bare hex at length 6 or 8, so any 8 hex digits become a color whose last two are alpha. `20261001` (a date) gets alpha 1/255 and looks like an empty bordered box; `48de7823` (a short hash) gets 0.14. **Impact:** cosmetic only (paste is unaffected), but dates, codes and short hashes are common clipboard contents.

**Suggested change:** require `#` for 8-digit hex as for 3/4-digit (`if (h.length === 8 && !hasHash) return null`), change the `'80ff0080'` test case to `'#80ff0080'`, and add a negative case such as `'20261001'`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 7cf67cb)</summary>

# Reproducer: bare 6- and 8-digit numbers and short hashes get a swatch

Reviewed commit: `7cf67cbc37ce73771cdc0c96817342f82c43862e` (also identical on a local merge into `quattro` `8b4eae66da2938ba9559f103b18dbf85cdf28a70`).

Save as `test/shell.d/clipboard-color-numbers-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/clipboard-color-numbers-test.sh`. It uses the same helpers (`run_node_test`, `requireFromRoot`, `assertEqual`) and the same `rgb8` helper as `test/shell.d/clipboard-color-test.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const color = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/clipboard/ColorParse.js')

function rgb8(text) {
  const c = color.parse(text)
  if (!c) return null
  return [Math.round(c.r * 255), Math.round(c.g * 255), Math.round(c.b * 255), Math.round(c.a * 100) / 100]
}

for (const text of ['482913', '20261001', '12345678', '48de7823']) console.log(`${text} -> ${JSON.stringify(rgb8(text))}`)

assertEqual(rgb8('20261001'), null, 'an eight-digit date is not a color')
assertEqual(rgb8('12345678'), null, 'an eight-digit number is not a color')
assertEqual(rgb8('48de7823'), null, 'an eight-character short commit hash is not a color')
JS
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (exit status 1):

```
482913 -> [72,41,19,1]
20261001 -> [32,38,16,0]
12345678 -> [18,52,86,0.47]
48de7823 -> [72,222,120,0.14]
expected: null
actual:   32,38,16,0
not ok - an eight-digit date is not a color
```

Notes:
- `rgb8` rounds alpha to two decimals; the real alpha for `20261001` is 1/255 (`0x01`). In an offscreen QML harness built from the PR's own delegate, that row's swatch color is `#01202610`: an almost fully transparent fill inside the 1 px border, so it looks like an empty box.
- `482913` (a 6-digit one-time code) is shown to illustrate the 6-digit case. That case is a trade-off: excluding all-digit 6-character strings would also drop grays such as `000000` or `333333` copied from design tools.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- Parser output matches color.js on 47 of 50 valid inputs in the documented forms (two of the other three are color.js errors, the third is the negative-chroma case below) and the spec's 12 oklab/oklch examples within 2/255; out-of-gamut colors are clipped per channel, as the code comment says; the Oklab matrices match Ottosson's reference.
- In an offscreen QML harness using the PR's delegate, the swatch appears only on color text rows; image, file and plain-text rows lay out exactly as at the merge base.
- `clipboard-color-test.sh` passes through `test/shell` (28 ok) and fails without the change; the full runner shows no new failures.
- The PR merges cleanly into current `quattro`; the clipboard tests, parser probe and QML harness give the same results there.

**Optional notes:**
- Spec edge cases (unlikely clipboard values): negative `oklch()` chroma is not clamped to 0 (`oklch(0.7 -0.1 200)` gives a reddish swatch instead of gray), lightness 1 with chroma gives a tint instead of white because channels are clipped rather than gamut-mapped, and commas in `oklab()`/`oklch()`, mixed separators or a slash-less fourth value are accepted. The test's `'hsla(0.5turn 50% 50%, 0.8)'` case is one such non-CSS form.
- Overlaps: open PR #9892 implements the same feature and conflicts with this PR at the delegate `swatchColor` property and the Text width; both PRs add a property of that name and their own swatch, so maintainers would pick one approach (or combine this parser with #9892's preview pane). #9662 conflicts at the same two lines, and a combined Text width needs to subtract both the star and the swatch.
</details>
